_about: Corpus for scripts/checker-truth-check.mjs (plan item 13). Made-up data and generic labels only. For each script, `elements` names the claim that owns the comparison of each text element the REAL figure draws (from scripts/truth/mpl_truth.py): C = control (the size comes from plt.rcParams['font.size'] or its update() dict form, or from ax.set_xlabel/set_ylabel/set_title(fontsize=) and ax.tick_params(labelsize=), all of which the checker is meant to read; must agree or the run exits 2), T = tick labels inheriting font.size (the 0.83x multiplier), W2 = a per-element rcParams key, SA = the rcParams alias (mpl.rcParams, from matplotlib import rcParams), SR = plt.rc(), SK = a fontsize= keyword the parser does not read, SK2 = a further keyword idiom (size=, fontdict=, a named size in fontsize=/labelsize=, legend(prop=), Text.set_fontsize), READTIME = an rcParams key set after the figure exists, G = Postr's own generated code (charts/codegen/toPython.ts) sets it through a variable. '-' = drawn but not scored (a mismatch there would be confounded by another claim, or belongs to another plan item). `what` says what the script exercises; it is documentation, not an input to the scoring. A script with `generated` is not a file here: the harness generates it at run time through the app's own module (`generated.module`, export `generated.export`) from `generated.spec`, so it always matches the shipped generator. `scaleClaim` names the claim that owns the scale comparison: C (the default, a control), G (G-scale: the canvas is set through variables), CANVAS (the canvas is not a literal figsize), '-' (not scored). `expect` makes the script a known answer (control K-known) for the claims it names: {claim: {observed, ofAtLeast}} - the claim's own comparison must observe exactly `observed` of at least `ofAtLeast`, and the script is kept out of that claim's k of n. Legend titles and Axes texts (claim AXTEXT), bbox_inches='tight' (TIGHT) and show() (SHOWSAVE) need no entry: the harness reads them from the real render.

ctl-default.what: no size set at all (matplotlib defaults, font.size 10); also K-known for CANVAS: the literal-figsize twin of cv-default-canvas

w2-rc-all.what: font.size 16 with axes.labelsize 11, axes.titlesize 12, legend.fontsize 9, x/ytick.labelsize 9 (item form)

w2-rc-fixblock.what: only per-element keys, the shape of the checker's own fix block: axes.titlesize 28, axes.labelsize 26, x/ytick.labelsize 20, legend.fontsize 20

w2-rc-named.what: font.size 20 with x/ytick.labelsize 'x-small' and legend.fontsize 'small' (named sizes)

w2-rc-yonly.what: font.size 20 with only ytick.labelsize 9 (x ticks stay 20)

s-rc-elements.what: plt.rc('font', size=20); plt.rc('axes', labelsize=20, titlesize=22); plt.rc('xtick'/'ytick', labelsize=16)

s-kw-pyplot.what: pyplot keywords: plt.xlabel/ylabel(fontsize=9), plt.xticks/yticks(fontsize=7), plt.title(fontsize=11), plt.legend(fontsize=7)

s-kw-axlegend.what: ax.set_xlabel/set_ylabel(fontsize=12) and ax.tick_params(labelsize=10), which are read, and ax.legend(fontsize=7), which is not

s-kw-ticklabels.what: font.size 20 with ax.set_xticklabels(..., fontsize=8) and plt.setp(ax.get_yticklabels(), fontsize=8)

g-codegen-grouped.what: Postr's own Make-a-figure Python for a grouped bar chart, generated live: title/axis/tick sizes via variables (title_size, axis_title_size, axis_text_size) passed as fontsize=/labelsize=, canvas figsize=(fig_w, fig_h), legend inherits font.size

cv-default-canvas.what: ctl-default without its figsize: a bare plt.subplots(), so matplotlib's default 6.4 x 4.8 in canvas

cv-rc-figsize.what: plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (4, 3) and font.size 12; plt.subplots() without figsize

cv-set-size-inches.what: plt.subplots() without figsize, then fig.set_size_inches(7, 5) before saving

w2-rc-dictvar.what: per-element keys in a dict held in a variable: params = {...}; plt.rcParams.update(params) (labels 8, title 9, ticks and legend 7)

w2-rc-context.what: with plt.rc_context({...}): per-element keys (labels 9, title 10, ticks and legend 8) around the whole figure, saved inside the block

rt-rc-after-fig.what: plt.rcParams.update of per-element keys (22/22/20/20) AFTER plt.subplots(): matplotlib draws the title (set_title) and legend at the new sizes, the axis labels and ticks at the old (10). The ticks are not scored: they inherit font.size, so on main their mismatch is the 0.83x tick model (T) and cannot show READTIME; rt-fontsize-after-fig carries the tick case (checker 16.6 pt against a real 10 pt, which neither 0.83 x 10 nor 1.0 x 20 explains)

rt-fontsize-after-fig.what: plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 20 AFTER plt.subplots(): the title (24) and legend (20) follow it, the axis labels and ticks stay 10

ax-legend-title.what: ax.legend(title='Treatment arm'): a legend title (no row in the table; AXTEXT), default sizes otherwise

sk2-size-alias.what: set_xlabel/set_ylabel(..., size=9) and set_title(..., size=10): the size= alias of fontsize=

sk2-named-kw.what: font.size 16 with ax.tick_params(labelsize='x-small') and ax.legend(fontsize='x-small'): named sizes in keywords

sk2-setfontsize-loop.what: font.size 16, then lab.set_fontsize(7) for every x and y tick label

ax-annotations.what: ax.bar_label, ax.text('**') and a fig.text caption at the default size: Axes texts have no row (AXTEXT); the caption row's 0.83x model is T's cause, so it is not scored

run-oo-figure.what: object-oriented matplotlib with no pyplot import: fig = Figure(figsize=(8, 6)); ax = fig.subplots() (RUN: a fix written as plt.rcParams has no plt)

run-seaborn-only.what: seaborn only, no pyplot import: sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid') (the notebook context: sizes 12/11) and an axes-level barplot on the default canvas; seaborn's sizes are plan item 14, so they are not scored here (RUN, CANVAS)

tight-legend-outside.what: font.size 16, a legend outside the Axes and fig.savefig(..., bbox_inches='tight'): the saved image is wider than the canvas (TIGHT)

show-only.what: pyplot with plt.show() and no savefig: the corrected code gets its savefig appended after plt.show() (SHOWSAVE)

ctl-oo-figure-import.what: K-known for RUN: run-oo-figure plus import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, so a plt.rcParams fix has its name

ctl-raise-only.what: K-known for L: font.size 6 on an 8 x 6 in canvas, so every text is below its minimum at every print size used (at most 7.2 pt x 1.67 = 12 pt) and a fix can only raise it

ctl-sk2-agree.what: K-known for SK2: size=10, fontdict={'fontsize': 10}, set_title(size=12), legend(prop={'size': 10}), each equal to the default the element has anyway; ticks via tick_params(labelsize=10)

ctl-rt-agree.what: K-known for READTIME: rcParams set after plt.subplots() to the values they have anyway (title 12, labels 10, legend 10), so when they are read cannot matter

ctl-axtext-large.what: K-known for AXTEXT: a legend title and an ax.text at 36 pt (27 pt at the smallest scale used), default sizes otherwise so a fix is offered

ctl-tight-full.what: K-known for TIGHT and TIGHT-fix: an invisible frame over the whole 8 x 6 in canvas and everything else inside it, saved with bbox_inches='tight', pad_inches=0, so the image written is the canvas

ctl-save-then-show.what: K-known for SHOWSAVE: plt.savefig() before plt.show(), so the inline backend saves the figure before show() closes it

ctl-w2-agree.what: K-known for W2: font.size 20 with axes.titlesize 24, axes.labelsize 20 and legend.fontsize 20 (rcParams.update), each the size the element has anyway; ticks via ax.tick_params(labelsize=20)

ctl-sa-agree.what: K-known for SA: plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 20 and then mpl.rcParams['font.size'] = 20, the alias setting the value font.size already has; ticks via ax.tick_params(labelsize=20)

ctl-sr-agree.what: K-known for SR: font.size 20 with plt.rc('font', size=20), plt.rc('axes', titlesize=24, labelsize=20), plt.rc('legend', fontsize=20), each the size the element has anyway; ticks via ax.tick_params(labelsize=20)

ctl-sk-agree.what: K-known for SK: font.size 20 with plt.xlabel/ylabel(fontsize=20), plt.title(fontsize=24), plt.legend(fontsize=20), each the size the element has anyway; ticks via plt.tick_params(labelsize=20)
